sections.h2: How do Hilliard homeowners usually sell, and what sets this city apart?
sections.html:
Hilliard homeowners can list through an agent, market the house on their own, or take an offer from a buyer who pays cash and accepts the property as is. The city's strong school district, high incomes and mix of 1950s subdivisions, Old Hilliard blocks and newer neighborhoods make it a place where condition and presentation drive the price.

Sellers here deal with Hilliard's planning staff on zoning and exterior rules, with the Franklin County Auditor on the deed, and with Ohio's disclosure statute. The sections below walk through each, along with the Census figures that describe who is buying.

sections.h2: What is Hilliard's history and where does it sit in Franklin County?
sections.html:
Hilliard sits in western Franklin County between Big Darby Creek and the Scioto River, bordered by Columbus, Upper Arlington, Dublin and Galloway. John Reed Hilliard bought about 10 acres of farmland in 1852 and platted the town on September 1, 1853 around a Piqua and Indiana Railroad station, so the place started as Hilliard's Station.

The village incorporated on July 13, 1869 with 280 residents. Three large subdivisions in the 1950s set off rapid growth, and Hilliard reached city status on December 12, 1960 with 5,633 people. Hookups to the regional water and sewer systems in the 1960s and the finished I-270 Outerbelt in the early 1970s drove a second wave.

The historic district along Norwich Street preserves older houses, and the restored original train station stands in Weaver Park. Cemetery Road and Main Street (Hilliard Rome Road) carry most local traffic, and I-270 reaches the city's eastern edge, with a park and ride on Cemetery Road close to the interchange.

Community landmarks include the Early Television Museum, the Franklin County Fair, the Old Hilliardfest art and street fair, a Fourth of July parade and the summer Celebration at the Station concerts. Buyers who tour the city often see those events, so a house within reach of Old Hilliard or a park carries that appeal into its listing.

sections.h2: What do the latest Census numbers say about Hilliard housing?
sections.html:
Hilliard has the highest median household income and home value of the four Ohio cities in the Census comparison used for these pages. A buyer pool with that profile expects clean, updated houses and will compare yours with newer construction in the same school zone.

sections.h2: Which schools and services cover a Hilliard address?
sections.html:
The Hilliard City School District covers the city, the old Brown and Norwich township areas, part of Columbus, and sections of Dublin and Galloway. It runs fourteen elementary schools, two sixth-grade schools (Station and Tharp), three middle schools (Heritage, Weaver and Memorial) and three high schools: Darby, Davidson and Bradley.

Saint Brendan School (K-8, Roman Catholic) and Sunrise Academy (K-8, Islamic) are in the city too. Because the district reaches past the city line, ask the district which school your exact address feeds.

  • Hilliard's own police division also patrols Norwich Township.
  • Norwich Township Fire Department provides fire and medical response for the city.
  • The recreation department manages more than 25 parks, and the Heritage Rail Trail starts on Center Street in Old Hilliard.
  • Voters approved a 0.5% income tax increase in November 2021 to pay for a recreation and wellness campus, backed by bonds of up to $95 million.

sections.h2: Which Hilliard planning rules should a seller check?
sections.html:
The Planning Division enforces Hilliard's zoning and property maintenance code and handles zoning certificates, property inspections, sign and fence permits, and zoning violation reports. Applications and fees go through the city's OpenGov portal.

The city warns that scammers email residents posing as city staff and demand payment for permits. Fees are paid only through the portal on an application you started, and the city does not send surprise invoices.

If you have rented the house, read the short-term rental rules first. City council amended chapters 1105, 1115, 1121 and 1141 on July 11, 2022 after finding that short-term rentals were not a permitted use, and the change tested the use in Old Hilliard with a review planned one year later. Ask the Planning Division what applies to your parcel today. The Planning Division page has contact details.

sections.h2: What does Ohio require a Hilliard seller to disclose?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires a completed state disclosure form for most sales of residential property with one to four dwelling units. You give each prospective buyer a signed, dated copy as soon as practicable, and the buyer signs to acknowledge it.

  • Topics include water and sewage systems, structure, hazardous materials and known material defects.
  • The form is not a warranty, and buyers are urged to get their own inspection.
  • You are not liable for an error you had no actual knowledge of.

Transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, between co-owners, from a government body, or to a buyer who has lived in the house for a year are exempt. See the full text.

sections.h2: What happens at the Franklin County Auditor when a Hilliard house sells?
sections.html:
Before the Auditor stamps a Hilliard deed, the buyer or the buyer's representative files a statement of value under R.C. 319.202. The seller pays the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax. Value means the full price paid, counting the mortgage balance the buyer takes on, and it is a violation to falsify it.

  • The statement asks whether the seller expects a property tax reduction under R.C. 323.152 to carry over to the buyer, and whether the land was in the agricultural use program.
  • Cash, business checks and cashier's checks payable to the Franklin County Auditor are accepted. Personal checks are not.
  • The exact payment must be presented or the transfer will not process.

The county's fee calculator sets out the rate. Your closing agent usually walks the deed through.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for a Hilliard property?
sections.html: A cash sale appeals when you cannot afford repairs before listing, need to close on a set date, or inherited a house you do not want to manage. A traditional sale fits a well-kept home in a school zone buyers like, and Hilliard's income levels mean many buyers arrive with financing and expect an inspection. Whatever you pick, compare the net proceeds after repairs and carrying costs and keep the written terms in front of you, including who pays for what at closing.

faqs.q: Is a short-term rental allowed at a Hilliard house?
faqs.a: Ask the Planning Division. Hilliard found in 2022 that short-term rentals were not a permitted use and amended its zoning code that July to test them in Old Hilliard. The rules for your parcel may depend on its zoning.

faqs.q: Which agency issues Hilliard zoning permits?
faqs.a: The Planning Division, through the city's OpenGov portal. It covers zoning certificates, sign and fence permits and inspections. Pay only through the portal, because the city says it does not email unexpected invoices.

faqs.q: Who provides fire service to a house in Hilliard?
faqs.a: Norwich Township Fire Department covers the city and the township. Hilliard's own police division also patrols the township.

faqs.q: Does a Hilliard buyer need to file anything with the county before the deed is stamped?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer or the buyer's representative submits a value statement to the Franklin County Auditor under R.C. 319.202, and the fee is paid before the Auditor endorses the deed.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a disclosure form if the buyer lived in my house first?
faqs.a: No. A transfer to someone who has occupied the property as a personal residence for at least one year before the transfer is exempt under R.C. 5302.30, as are transfers to family and between co-owners.
